image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a compact audio cassette tape. The casing appears to be made of translucent or semi-opaque plastic with a bluish-purple tint. Two circular spool hubs are visible on the left and right, connected by a strip of magnetic tape across the center window. There is a label area in the middle and text printed directly on the plastic casing above and below the window. The bottom edge shows the rectangular opening for the tape head and write-protect tabs.

artifact_observations.location: Top and bottom edges of the cassette face
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text printed on the casing is nonsensical, distorted, and unreadable, resembling alien script or melted characters rather than legible alphanumeric text.
The plastic surface has a smeared, painterly texture rather than the smooth, reflective quality of molded plastic. There are subtle inconsistencies in the transparency.
The bottom edge lacks crisp definition. The write-protect tabs are not clearly defined as movable physical parts but appear fused into the casing body.
The rectangular window appears slightly warped and not perfectly parallel to the outer edges, suggesting minor geometric instability.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly identified as a cassette and not a similar rectangular object.
To analyze the illegible/gibberish text artifacts on the casing and label area.
To check for boundary bleeding between the plastic casing and the background, and ensure the spools are contained within the shell.
To assess the overall texture quality and identify any subtle melting or smoothing artifacts typical of AI generation.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of printed text
Definition of mechanical parts (write-protect tabs, screw holes)
Transparency and refraction logic of the plastic casing
Geometric symmetry of the spool windows
